title: Decision
description: Structured skeleton of a decision. Reasoning lives in the 'rationale' free-form text and cited artifacts. The structured fields exist only for pre-registration integrity, post-hoc audit, and replay — not to constrain how the decision is reached.

candidate_claims.description: Set of claims the decision arbitrated between. Cardinality 1 is normal; cardinality >1 represents contention (scarce realization slot, multi-instance capital contention, etc.).

chosen_claim_id.description: The claim selected by this decision. MUST be a member of candidate_claims.

successor_claim_id.description: Optional. When kind='pivot' or 'kill' and a successor Claim is opened to continue the investigation under a revised frame, this points to that successor. The successor MUST be a new immutable Claim with its own role_declared_at (not a mutation). This is how hypothesis lineage is preserved across regime shifts and pivots without violating Claim immutability.

rationale.description: Free-form. Why this candidate was not chosen.

rejected_alternatives.description: Required when candidate_claims has > 1 entry. The arbitration objective itself is free-form text (see 'arbitration' below).

arbitration.description: Required when candidate_claims has > 1 entry. Captures the arbitration move without prescribing HOW it was reasoned. The objective field is free-form; structure is only on what was compared and in what order.

objective.description: Free-form statement of the arbitration objective (e.g., 'maximize risk-adjusted expected return over 90d, subject to correlated-exposure ceiling').

tie_break_order.description: Ordered list of tie-break criteria applied. Free-form strings.

governing_policy_ids.description: Policies that bounded the arbitration (e.g., correlated-exposure ceiling).

cited_evidence.description: Evidence ids cited by this decision. Evidence with polarity='contradicts' known at decision time MUST be cited.

contradiction_operator.description: Free-form: what detected the contradiction (e.g., 'regime-mismatch check', 'human flag', 'statistical test X'). Optional — narrative detection is valid.

rationale.description: Free-form reasoning trail. This is where the agent actually argues; the structured fields record what was pre-registered and what was emitted, not how the agent thought.

policies_in_force.description: Resolved Policy id + version effective at decision time for every governed field touched. minItems:1 is canon working as designed (obligation 7: a Decision governed by no policy is unanswerable) — do not relax it. For terminal decisions, validator rule 13 additionally requires that EVERY frozen Policy bound to the chosen Claim appear here: citing only the gate you passed is cherry-picking a pre-registration.

policy_rollback.description: Required when kind=rollback_policy. Makes rollback precedence mechanically replayable.

fired_rule_ids.description: All rollback rules whose conditions fired at evaluation time (not just the winner).

precedence_winner.description: The rule id selected by the Policy.rollback_rule.precedence ordering.

rejected_amendment_ids.description: Any in-flight amend_policy Decision ids that were rejected by this rollback.

allOf.description: Contention integrity: when there is more than one candidate claim, rejected_alternatives and arbitration are required. Validators MUST additionally check: chosen_claim_id ∈ candidate_claims; rejected_alternatives.claim_ids ∪ {chosen_claim_id} == candidate_claims (set equality); no duplicates. (JSON Schema cannot express set-equality against a sibling array; this is a canon-validator rule recorded in canon.md.)
